saints.name: Ninian of Whithorn
saints.dates: About 360–432 in the published GOARCH parish life

summary.text: A British bishop associated with Whithorn and the Christian mission among the southern Picts. Both GOARCH and ROCOR publications commemorate him.
summary.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

saints.context: The Church's published hagiographic account is distinguished from independently established chronology. Unknown dates and circumstances are left unspecified.

blocks.text: The parish life places his birth around 360 in Cumberland, in a Christian family. It describes a period of study and ascetic life in Rome.
blocks.locator: Ninian the Enlightener of Scotland, opening biographical sentences

blocks.text: After episcopal consecration, he returned to Britain toward the end of the fourth century. The life associates him with monasteries, preaching among Britons and Picts, and a cathedral at Whithorn dedicated to Saint Martin.

blocks.text: The published life records peaceful repose at Whithorn in 432. ROCOR’s liturgical index likewise lists that year; these are attributed traditional dates.

blocks.text: The ROCOR index identifies him as bishop of Whithorn and apostle to the southern Picts, commemorated on September 16. It records services in both English and Greek.
